summary: This note contains the general terms of sale for U.S. Department of the Treasury real property auctions run by CWS Asset Management & Sales (CWSAMS) as agent for the Government. It covers how binding contracts form when a bid is accepted, bidder eligibility and registration rules, inspection, written and online bidding procedures, deposits, closing, title deed types, defaults, and compliance duties. The terms state that properties are sold as-is and that no financing is provided.
one_line: General terms of sale for U.S. Treasury real property auctions run by CWS Marketing Group, covering bidding, deposits, closing, title and defaults.
key_facts: A successful bid at a Department of the Treasury auction establishes a legally binding contract between the successful bidder and the Government, subject to final acceptance by the government.
CWSAMS (CWS Asset Management & Sales), the Contractor, acts as the agent of the Government in selling Government real property at these auctions.
Bidders must present a valid government issue photo ID and evidence of earnest money deposit as a prerequisite of registration.
CWS Marketing Group, Inc. does not accept personal or business checks, money orders, credit cards, or cash.
Written bids must be received no later than 5:00 p.m. on the date specified at CWS Marketing Group, 7998 Donegan Drive, Manassas, VA 20109.
Online high bidder must deliver ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price less the initial money deposit, whichever is greater, within three business days.
In online auctions, a bid placed in the last 1-minute extends the lot's end time by 1-minute.
Property is offered AS IS and WITH ALL FAULTS, and the Government makes no warranties regarding quality, condition or habitability.
Closing will be held within 45 calendar days of the date the Government signs the sales contract accepting the Buyer's offer.
This is a cash sale, and the Government does not provide financing for the purchase of any property.
A Government Deed, Special Warranty Deed, or Quit Claim Deed conveys title at closing, depending on the sale.
Forfeited real property will not be sold to the defendant or person(s) acting as his/her agent, per 18 USC Section 1963(f) and 21 USC Section 853(h).
Failure to make required deposit or final payments within the specified time frames is deemed default of the high bidder and may result in forfeiture of the deposit.
Bidders registered to bid for a corporation, business, or LLC must provide appropriate official documentation of eligibility.
The minimum reserve price is not released to the public.
